Metabolic & GLP-1 in Canada — What Every Listing Shows

The incretin class covers compounds that act at the GLP-1 receptor and, in the newer molecules, at the GIP and glucagon receptors alongside it. The published research on this group is unusually deep for a research-peptide category: semaglutide and tirzepatide both carry large named clinical programmes, and retatrutide — a triple agonist — has phase 2 data in the literature under its own compound code.

This category groups the single, dual and triple receptor agonists together with the amylin analogues, because the research questions overlap. Cagrilintide and eloralintide are studied at the amylin receptor rather than the incretin receptors, and appear here for that reason. Orforglipron sits in the same collection despite being a non-peptide small molecule, since it is characterised as an orally available GLP-1 receptor agonist.

Every lot in this category is independently assayed before it is released. The batch identifier, the measured purity and the measured content are printed on the product card and on the certificate itself, so the numbers are visible before anything is added to a cart rather than after delivery. All compounds are supplied strictly as laboratory research materials.

records.title: Semaglutide
records.description:
Semaglutide is a synthetic analogue of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), a naturally occurring incretin hormone involved in glucose-dependent signaling. It is developed for controlled laboratory investigation within regulated experimental environments.
In scientific literature, semaglutide is studied in experimental models examining GLP-1 receptor activation pathways, incretin-related signaling cascades, and downstream endocrine regulatory dynamics under in vitro and preclinical research conditions.
Overview
Semaglutide is a synthetic, long-acting analogue of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) evaluated in research focused on incretin receptor signaling activity. As a compound structurally engineered to interact with GLP-1 receptor systems with extended half-life, it is studied within experimental models examining receptor-driven signaling pathways and metabolic regulatory interaction.
Preclinical and clinical research publications have explored its receptor-binding profile, downstream pathway activation, and GLP-1 receptor signaling dynamics under controlled study conditions.
History
GLP-1 was identified during investigations into incretin hormone physiology and glucose-dependent insulin secretion. Early research established it as a short-acting endogenous signaling peptide, with subsequent investigations focused on developing structurally modified analogues with improved stability and extended receptor interaction profiles.
Semaglutide emerged from this lineage as a long-acting GLP-1 analogue incorporating structural modifications — including a C-18 fatty acid side chain and backbone substitutions — designed to enhance albumin binding and resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 degradation within experimental systems.
Research
Laboratory investigations into semaglutide have focused on GLP-1 receptor activation models and downstream incretin signaling pathways. Research frameworks evaluate receptor-mediated interaction, endocrine regulatory dynamics, and metabolic signaling mechanisms under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.

records.title: Eloralintide
records.description:
This product is supplied as eloralintide (LY3841136), a long-acting, selective amylin receptor agonist studied in research on metabolic and body-weight regulation.
Note that no compound named "elaronitide" appears in PubMed, PubChem, or the INN register. The vial artwork spelling appears to be in error.
Overview
Eloralintide is a selective agonist of the AMY1 amylin receptor, engineered with a fatty-diacid conjugate that supports albumin binding and an extended half-life. Research has characterized its selectivity for AMY1R over the calcitonin receptor and other amylin receptor subtypes.
Clinical research has evaluated the compound across phase 1 and phase 2 programmes, examining amylin-pathway pharmacology and body-weight endpoints under controlled conditions.
History
Eloralintide was developed as part of research into amylin-pathway agonists as an alternative to incretin-based mechanisms for metabolic regulation. Discovery and early characterization work described its receptor selectivity and long-acting design.
Subsequent phase 1 and phase 2 studies characterized its pharmacological profile in obesity research populations.
Research
Research into eloralintide focuses on selective amylin receptor activation and its metabolic consequences. Frameworks evaluate receptor-subtype selectivity, pharmacokinetics of the long-acting design, and body-weight endpoints under controlled clinical conditions.

records.title: AOD-9604
records.description:

AOD-9604 reproduces the lipolytic domain of human growth hormone while lacking the regions associated with insulin-like growth effects. Research has examined its action on lipid metabolism, including stimulation of lipolysis and inhibition of lipogenesis in cellular and animal models.
Studies have also evaluated its profile in cartilage and joint research models under structured conditions.
History
AOD-9604 was developed from research mapping the lipolytic activity of growth hormone to its C-terminal fragment. The synthetic peptide was characterized to retain fat-metabolism activity independent of GH receptor growth signaling.
Subsequent studies investigated metabolic and musculoskeletal research applications.
Research
Research into AOD-9604 focuses on lipid-metabolism and GH-fragment models. Frameworks evaluate lipolytic and antilipogenic signaling and musculoskeletal endpoints under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.

mainEntity.name: Are GLP-1 research peptides legal to buy in Canada?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are supplied here strictly as laboratory research materials, and are sold on that basis. None of the compounds in this category is approved by Health Canada in this form for diagnosis, treatment or prevention of any condition, and nothing on this site describes human use. The approved medicines that share an active ingredient with some of these compounds are separate, prescription-only products from their originator manufacturers.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between retatrutide, tirzepatide and semaglutide?

acceptedAnswer.text: The number of receptors each one is characterised as acting at. Semaglutide is described in the literature as a single GLP-1 receptor agonist; tirzepatide as a dual agonist at GLP-1 and GIP; retatrutide as a triple agonist adding the glucagon receptor. That difference is structural and is the reason the three are studied against one another rather than interchangeably. The comparison guides linked from this page set out what the published trials report for each.

mainEntity.name: Why are cagrilintide and eloralintide in the same category?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are amylin receptor agonists rather than incretin agonists, so mechanistically they sit apart from the GLP-1 group. They are collected here because the research questions overlap — the published work studies them alongside and in combination with incretin compounds rather than in isolation.

mainEntity.name: What is published for each lot in this category?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lot code, the HPLC purity figure and the measured content against the labelled amount, plus the issuing laboratory and its test date. All of it is on the product card before anything is added to a cart, and the full certificate is linked from the lot code so the numbers can be read in the laboratory’s own report rather than in our summary of it.
